title: Molecular Brownian Motion Gas Simulation
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D molecular Brownian motion gas simulation using Three.js (CDN). The simulation models ideal gas particles in a bounded cubic container with elastic collisions.

## Scene Setup
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 0, 45), looking at origin, FOV 60.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light at (10, 20, 15) with intensity 0.8.
- Create a wireframe cube container of side length 20 (from -10 to +10 on each axis) using EdgesGeometry + LineSegments with color #44aaff, semi-transparent.
- OrbitControls for camera rotation.

## Particles
- Start with 80 spherical particles (radius 0.3, IcosahedronGeometry detail 1).
- Each particle gets a random initial position inside the container (uniform random in [-9, 9] on each axis).
- Each particle gets a random initial velocity vector. Speed magnitude drawn uniformly from [1, 4]. Direction random on unit sphere.
- Color particles by speed: slow (< 1.5) = blue (#3366ff), medium (1.5-3.0) = green (#33ff66), fast (> 3.0) = red (#ff3333). Update colors every frame.
- Store particles as an array of objects: { mesh, velocity: {x,y,z}, mass: 1.0 }.

## Physics
- Use a fixed timestep of dt = 0.016 per frame for integration.
- Wall collisions: when a particle center reaches ±(10 - 0.3), reflect the corresponding velocity component (elastic wall bounce). Clamp position inside bounds.
- Particle-particle collisions: check pairwise distances. If distance < 0.6 (2*radius), perform elastic collision using conservation of momentum and kinetic energy for equal-mass particles (swap velocity components along collision normal). Separate overlapping particles.
- Compute total kinetic energy each frame: sum of 0.5 * mass * |v|^2 for all particles. This should be approximately conserved (within 1% of initial value).
- Compute average speed, min speed, max speed each frame.
- Gravity toggle: when enabled, add gravity acceleration (0, -5, 0) per frame to each particle velocity. Default: OFF.

## Temperature Control
- A 'temperature' parameter (range 0.2 to 5.0, default 1.0) that scales all particle speeds.
- When temperature changes, multiply each particle velocity by (newTemp / oldTemp) ratio.
- Provide a slider in the HUD labeled 'Temperature' that adjusts this.

## User Interactions
- Press SPACE to toggle pause/resume of the simulation.
- Press G to toggle gravity on/off.
- Press R to reset all particles to new random positions and velocities.
- Press A to add 10 more particles (up to max 200).
- Press D to remove 10 particles (down to min 10).
- Temperature slider (HTML range input) from 0.2 to 5.0, step 0.1.
- A 'Show Trails' checkbox that toggles short trailing lines behind each particle (last 8 positions).

## HUD / UI
- Top-left overlay panel (semi-transparent dark background, white text, monospace font) showing:
  - Particle Count
  - Average Speed (2 decimal places)
  - Total Kinetic Energy (2 decimal places)
  - Temperature value
  - Gravity status (ON/OFF)
  - Paused status (YES/NO)
  - FPS counter
- Temperature slider below the stats.
- 'Show Trails' checkbox below the slider.

## State Management (CRITICAL)
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame with:
  - particleCount: number of active particles
  - averageSpeed: average speed of all particles (number)
  - totalKineticEnergy: sum of 0.5*m*v^2 for all particles (number)
  - initialKineticEnergy: the total KE computed right after initialization or reset (number)
  - temperature: current temperature value (number)
  - gravityEnabled: boolean
  - paused: boolean
  - showTrails: boolean
  - frameCount: integer incremented each simulation step
  - minSpeed: minimum particle speed (number)
  - maxSpeed: maximum particle speed (number)
  - wallBounceCount: cumulative number of wall bounces since last reset (number)
  - particleCollisionCount: cumulative number of particle-particle collisions since last reset (number)
  - particles: array of { x, y, z, vx, vy, vz, speed } for each particle
  - containerSize: 20 (the side length)
  - energyConservationRatio: totalKineticEnergy / initialKineticEnergy (number, should be ~1.0 without gravity)

Ensure the simulation runs smoothly at 60fps. Use requestAnimationFrame. All code in one HTML file, no external dependencies except Three.js and OrbitControls from CDN.
physics_constraints: Elastic collisions conserve total kinetic energy (within 1% tolerance without gravity). Wall reflections are perfectly elastic. Particles must remain within the cubic container bounds [-10, 10]. Particle-particle collisions use equal-mass elastic collision formulas along the collision normal. When gravity is off, energy conservation ratio should stay in [0.99, 1.01].
